market_context: United States/international; opened refrigerated tofu and household storage.
title: How Long Does Opened Tofu Last in the Refrigerator?

seo.title: How Long Does Opened Tofu Last in the Fridge?
seo.meta_description: A practical household window for opened refrigerated tofu is about 3–5 days at 40°F or below. Store it in a clean covered container; if it came in water, fresh water changed daily can help quality. Sour odor, slime, or abnormal color mean discard.
seo.search_intent: Understand how many days opened tofu keeps, how to store it in water or without water, what spoilage signs matter, and when freezing makes sense.

excerpt: Once opened, refrigerated tofu has a much shorter window than the sealed package. A practical household reference is about 3–5 days at 40 °F (4 °C) or below. If the tofu came packed in water, storing leftovers covered with fresh clean water and changing it daily can help prevent drying and off odors. Sour smell, slime, or abnormal discoloration are discard signs.
content_html:
Once opened, refrigerated tofu is best treated as a short-lived perishable food, with roughly 3–5 refrigerated days as a practical household reference. The sealed package can last much longer because it was processed and filled under controlled conditions.

The exact window depends on the product. Water-packed refrigerated tofu, shelf-stable aseptic tofu, smoked tofu, and marinated products are not identical, so package instructions take priority.

Why opening shortens the storage window

Opening exposes tofu to oxygen, hands, utensils, and environmental microorganisms. Its high water activity and nutrient content make it a good spoilage environment once the package barrier is gone.

Refrigeration slows microbial growth but does not stop it.

This is why the original date printed for an unopened package should not automatically be used as the after-opening deadline.

If it came in water, store it in fresh clean water

A common household method is to move leftover tofu to a clean container, cover it with potable water, and refrigerate it with a lid.

Changing that water daily helps limit stale odors and keeps the tofu from drying out.

Use clean hands and utensils. Changing the water does not restart the storage clock; the tofu itself is still aging.

Shelf-stable and refrigerated tofu differ before opening

Some aseptically packaged tofu can remain at room temperature while sealed. Once it is opened, leftovers must be refrigerated.

Tofu sold from the refrigerated case should stay refrigerated even before opening unless the manufacturer clearly states otherwise.

After opening, both products become moist perishable foods that should be used within a few days.

What spoilage signs matter?

Abnormally sour or fermented odor, a very slimy surface, unusual pink, yellow, or brown discoloration, gas, or mold are reasons to discard tofu.

Fresh tofu usually has a mild aroma. If the change is obvious, do not taste a bite to decide whether it is still acceptable.

Pathogens do not always produce sensory warning signs, so time and temperature still matter when the tofu looks normal.

Time out of refrigeration counts too

Tofu is perishable. Return leftovers to refrigeration within two hours during ordinary conditions, or one hour when ambient temperature is above 90 °F (32 °C).

A container that sat on a table for several hours does not become safe again simply because it goes back into the refrigerator.

Keep the refrigerator at 40 °F or below and avoid the warm, variable door area when possible.

Freezing is useful if you will not finish it

Tofu freezes safely and FoodKeeper uses a multi-month quality window, but the texture changes dramatically: thawed tofu becomes more porous and chewy.

If that texture suits your recipe, freezing portions is better than stretching refrigerator storage.

Freeze while the tofu is still fresh and thaw later under refrigeration.

Make the date visible

Write the opening date on the storage container. That is more reliable than trying to remember when the original package was first used.

If the label says to use within three days, follow that instruction. If it gives no after-opening guidance, about 3–5 refrigerated days is a practical benchmark.

The practical rule: use opened tofu within a few days, keep it very cold and clean, and change the water daily if you store it submerged. If you will not finish it in time, freeze it before quality declines.

faq.question: How many days does opened tofu last?
faq.answer: A practical household reference is about 3–5 days refrigerated at 40°F or below unless the package gives a shorter time.

faq.question: Should you change tofu storage water?
faq.answer: If you store tofu submerged, use fresh potable water and change it daily. This helps quality but does not reset the storage time.

faq.question: How can you tell tofu has gone bad?
faq.answer: Abnormal sour odor, slime, clear discoloration, gas, or mold are reasons to discard it.
